note: Attacker-controlled bytes from the incoming NCP frame are exposed as a null-terminated string (networkName). There is no length cap beyond the frame size, so an over-long network name enters the stack.
The decoded network name (32 bytes here) is fetched from the spinel PROP_VALUE_SET payload for SPINEL_PROP_MESHCOP_COMMISSIONER_GENERATE_PSKC and forwarded to the PSKc generation API.
The public API passes the attacker-controlled network name unchanged into MeshCoP::Commissioner::GeneratePskc.
Fixed-size 30-byte stack buffer for the PBKDF2 salt: 6-byte 'Thread' prefix + 8-byte extended PAN ID + up to 16-byte network name.

Root cause: the only input validation performed before the salt copy bounds the passphrase length; aNetworkName length is never checked against OT_NETWORK_NAME_MAX_SIZE (16), so an over-long name is allowed to reach the fixed-size salt buffer.
Salt is filled to offset 14 (6-byte prefix at line 1115 plus 8-byte extended PAN ID), leaving only 16 bytes of capacity for the network name.
Sink: strlen(aNetworkName) (32) bytes are copied at salt+14 into the 30-byte buffer; 16 bytes are written past the end of salt, causing the stack-buffer-overflow.
